extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, students of fiction, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on methods of presenting novels—how to choose and manage point of view, the relation of character to environment, and when to use panoramic (pictorial) versus scenic (dramatic) presentation. Emphasises unity of vision, subtle authorial tone (irony/aloofness), and matching method to narrative needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and environment as joint subject
rubrics_metrics.description: What he proposes to exhibit is the history of a woman like her in just such a world as hers; the provincial scene, acting upon her, making her what she becomes, is as essential as she is herself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat protagonist and setting integrally — the environment should be as essential and fully realised as the central character, not merely a background. The novel's purpose may be to show how life in a particular milieu shapes a person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide drama versus pictorial emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Not a portrait, therefore, not a study of character for its own sake, but something in the nature of a drama... But then again — that is not exactly the question in this book... the emphasis is not upon the commonplace little events of Emma’s career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the work's primary aim is dramatic (conflict and outcome) or pictorial (impression/portrait). If pictorial, incidents serve illustration; if dramatic, incidents must be organised to produce an issue or climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use incidents to illustrate subject, not necessarily to drive plot
rubrics_metrics.description: The events, therefore... are only Flaubert’s way of telling his subject, of making it count to the eye. They are not in themselves what he has to say, they simply illustrate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events and episodes may be chosen as ways of showing the central impression; they need not be indispensable as plot points. Beware forcing every scene to be a turning-point when the aim is pictorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain unity of point of view / centre of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is to have that unity which it needs to produce its right effect there can be no uncertainty here, no arbitrary shifting of the place from which an onlooker faces it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide a centre of vision (from within a character or an authorial vantage) and avoid arbitrary or confusing shifts that break the novel's unity and diminish effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter character consciousness when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of his subject is Emma’s sense of her world; we must see how it impresses her and what she makes of it... For this reason it is essential to pass into her consciousness, to make her subjective; and Flaubert takes care to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the character's inner experience where the subject demands it so readers can share that point of view; but ensure this subjective material serves the book's larger purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide external authorial perception when protagonist’s view is inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Her intelligence is much too feeble and fitful to give a sufficient account of her world... The author's wit, therefore, and none other, must supply what is wanting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the protagonist cannot perceive or articulate essential aspects of the world, the author must supply that perception — but do so carefully to avoid disruptive shifts of stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make transitions of vision without awkwardness
rubrics_metrics.description: The transition must be made without awkwardness, without calling attention to it... There is nothing more disconcerting in a novel than to see the writer changing his part in this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hide or smooth changes between subjective and objective vantage points; avoid blatant authorial intrusions or noticeable role-switching that dislocate the reader's immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overt authorial intrusion unless stylistically intended
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps it is only Thackeray, among the great, who seems to find a positively wilful pleasure in damaging his own story by open maltreatment of this kind... to insist on his freedom to say what he pleases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate authorial asides or open maltreatment of the story can be a licence for some writers but generally risk damaging the narrative; use with conscious stylistic purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep protagonist at an authorially controlled distance
rubrics_metrics.description: He deals with the difficulty I have described by keeping Emma always at a certain distance, even when he appears to be entering her mind most freely... he does so with an air of aloofness that forbids us ever to become entirely identified with her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a measured distance (often via subtle irony or tone) so readers can observe a character's folly without becoming fully absorbed; this can preserve judgment and broader perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use irony subtly via tone rather than explicit assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: He knows it without asserting it... his valuation of her is only implied; it is in his tone — never in his words, which invariably respect her own estimate of herself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey the author's appraisal of characters indirectly through tone and implication rather than direct statements; respect characters' self-views in dialogue and interiority while the narrative tone can carry ironic distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render setting as distinct and individual as characters
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to be rendered, and in order to make it clearly tell beside the figure of Emma it must be as distinct and individual, as thoroughly characterized as she is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give towns, communities, and secondary types full, specific treatment — they should contribute integrally to the book's picture, not sit passively in the background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare alternative viewpoints for future revelation
rubrics_metrics.description: Charles must be held in readiness... his inner mind, and his point of view, must be created in advance and kept in reserve, so that the force of the climax... may be instantly felt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later climax depends on another character’s perception (e.g., a posthumous discovery), establish and reserve that perspective early so the payoff is credible and powerful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose between panoramic (panorama) and scenic presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: I start from that distinction between the 'panoramic' and the 'scenic' presentation of a story... Thackeray saw them as broad expanses, stretches of territory, to be surveyed from edge to edge with a sweeping glance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panoramic: use broad surveys, retrospective reminiscence, many typical characters to create an impression of manners or society. Scenic: focus on enacted scenes and dramatic particularity. Match the mode to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use panoramic method to evoke social/temporal impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Not in any complication of incident... is the subject of Vanity Fair to be discerned. It is... in the impression of a world, a society, a time... Thackeray preferred the manner of musing expatiation, where scene melts into scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the aim is an impression of society or manners, use leisurely, discursive reminiscence, foreshortening of detail, and fusion of instances to the broad effect rather than tightly plotted scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate particular incidents to a general effect in panoramic style
rubrics_metrics.description: That foreshortening and generalizing, that fusion of detail, that subordination of the instance and the occasion to the broad effect, are the elements of the pictorial art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow anecdotes and small incidents to serve the larger tone and panorama; a hint or brief glimpse often suffices — don't insist every episode be dramatically foregrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switch to scenic method for climactic enactment
rubrics_metrics.description: The final scene cannot be recalled and summarized in his indirect, reminiscential manner. It must be placed immediately before us... Now they must come forward, declare themselves, and be seen for what they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the narrative demands a decisive answer or climax, present it directly and dramatically in a full scene rather than summarizing; some moments require immediate enactment for proper force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match method to the narrative demand and be self-critical
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a book that with its variety of method, and with its careful restriction of that variety to its bare needs, and with its scrupulous use of its resources — it is a book, altogether, that gives a good point of departure for an examination of the methods of fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be deliberate about variety of method: restrict styles to what the story needs, and use resources scrupulously. Avoid applying a method where it weakens the required effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a consistent authorial standard through shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Very discreetly the same standard has reigned throughout. That is the way in which Flaubert’s impersonality, so called, artfully operates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when shifting between perspectives or moods, preserve a unifying standard or tone so the work feels coherent and avoids dislocation between conflicting values or voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create both subjective immediacy and external perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: We who read the book are to share her sense of life... we are to be placed within her world, to get the immediate taste of it, and outside her world as well, to get the full effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers with immersive access to a character's experience while also offering the external overview necessary to see the larger significance; balancing both yields fuller effect.
